Senses.Explanation: Nothing beyond one's own due. Chijue Daochong, retelling the rhino-fan case turn by turn and grading every ancient in it — Xuedou's head-and-horns, Shishuang's already-gone tail, Zifu's circle with an ox inside, Baofu's advice that the aged master get someone else — hears Xuedou pity the effort as wasted and drops his one-line verdict: nothing beyond his due; Lianyue Daozheng, when a lay patron describes the bared sword — demon kings' skulls split, foxes gone to ground — answers the exclamation with the same flat seal before opening his discern-demons demands; Huiyue Xu raises Gaofeng's held whisk — no step forward, no step back, nothing at all, and what is it that neither-nor — rules that Gaofeng spent nine oxen's strength and still could not turn his body, then announces that Jinming shaking out sinew and bone with the ancients is nothing beyond his due, and at once licenses forward, back, and neither-nor alike. Juyun Chuiwan Guangzhen, at the Buddha's birthday where everyone bathes the crown prince in fragrant soup, claims that his own two-drumhide clatter of vines pushing open the buddhas' knowledge inside the beings' realm is nothing beyond his due; Yinyuan Longqi dares guarantee that sitting astride the transformation-buddhas' heads and overturning the right-and-wrong nest — daily digesting ten thousand taels of gold — is nothing beyond his due; Hanxiu Ruqian, dissolving the retreat and asking each trainee whether the original-portion matter is penetrated, rules that whoever has penetrated may roam the western heaven by morning and return east by dusk, gods' games nothing beyond his due; Linye Tongqi, at his own mountain-gate inauguration, reads the ceremony to the radiant seated one — worship and incense, nothing beyond his due; and Liangting Jingting, standing before his dead dharma-brother's coffin, traces the five years of phoenix-peak music and the iron hawk rising from fire, then seals the whole lifelong use — this was what my dharma-brother used up his life on, and it too was nothing beyond his due.
